title: Autoresearch program and experiment protocol
author: Andrej Karpathy
version: master branch, public text inspected November 20, 2026
claims: The usage rules reserve train.py for changes and keep prepare.py and the evaluation fixed.
The loop redirects train output, then logs keep, discard or crash with the commit, score and memory.
A lower val_bpb advances the branch. An equal or higher value causes a revert.
limits: This is the stated protocol, with an open-ended loop. The local workshop uses a fixed candidate count. This source does not show that each proposed experiment improves performance.
evidence: Each experiment runs on a single GPU, constraints before Output format

title: Autoresearch training loop
author: Andrej Karpathy
version: master branch, public source inspected November 20, 2026
claims: The main loop measures synchronized steps, accumulates time after initial steps and breaks at TIME_BUDGET.
It calls evaluate_bpb after training and prints val_bpb, measured training time, total time and peak memory.
limits: Training time and total process time are separate. This workshop inspected the code and did not execute GPU training.
evidence: train.py main loop near lines 496 to 560
train.py final evaluation and printed summary near lines 565 to 583

title: Autoresearch fixed evaluation and budget
author: Andrej Karpathy
version: master branch, public source inspected November 20, 2026
claims: TIME_BUDGET is 300 seconds. evaluate_bpb reads validation batches, excludes zero-byte targets from the loss sum and divides accumulated nats by the byte count times log(2).
limits: This is a language-model loss metric calculated against validation data. It does not measure retrieval evidence or external validity.

title: BrowseComp, a benchmark for browsing agents
author: OpenAI
claims: BrowseComp contains 1,266 problems for finding difficult information with browsing agents.
The authors prefer questions with short, verifiable answers and describe their task selection.
limits: The benchmark concerns public web research. The local card exercise measures evidence retrieval on a fixed index and can be checked without a web connection.
